topics: KV cache warmup and perf regression
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood CSM joined late), Mark (CTO - Horizon), Priya (Infra), Daniel (ML), Sara (Security)

Summary: quick sync on the private VPC pilot. We wanted to cover the routing problem seen during last week's upgrade, verify KV cache metrics, and align on a window for a controlled rolling upgrade.

[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll give about 30 minutes of sync and then time for questions. Marco will join in about 10. Um, quick callout: we pulled logs overnight and there are a couple of routing anomalies to review.

[00:22] Priya (Infra): Yep, we saw two nodes drop during the upgrade, and traffic to the model pods started spiking 5xxs, not sure if that's a firewall rule or a route table issue.

[00:40] Sofia (Redwood SE): Right, from the traces we saw a couple of connections timing out to the cache layer — the K-V cash — and then the frontend retried and caused the token spool, so latency went up. Could be NAT timeouts or sticky SNAT mappings.

[01:10] Daniel (ML): Just to add, the ML infra noticed that when the KV cache miss rate jumps, throughput drops by roughly 20-30% on our test workload. We run a 64-128 token average in the bench.

[01:35] Mark (CTO): Are we confident this is network and not a model variant mismatch? We did switch from the quantized v2 to the v2a for the test.

[01:55] Sofia: Good question. We validated model binary and config — the kernel/quant bits match. The regression line up with the time window when the NAT gateway had a flappy route. So leaning network. But we'll confirm with the logs.

[02:20] Sara (Security): From SEC side, any change in egress means we need updated flow logs for our compliance review.

[02:35] Liam: Noted. Priya, can you share the VPC flow logs for the timeframe? That'll help us correlate packet drops vs pod restarts.

[02:50] Priya: Yeah, we'll pull them and send — expect by Friday. There was also manual firewall tweak around 02:00 UTC; I can include the change set.

[03:12] Sofia: Thanks. On the Redwood side, we ran a short repro in staging where we artificially induced NAT port exhaustion. We observed exactly the K-V cache miss pattern, then the reroute to fallback model variant. There's some noisy retries from the client side that amplify the problem.

[03:45] Daniel: The fallbacks make sense; we saw increased calls to the cheaper Llama-compat model when the primary timed out. That explains the quality dip.

[04:05] Mark: Ok, so what's the plan for the next production rolling upgrade? We need a clear pre-checklist.

[04:18] Liam: Good — we propose a two-step plan: 1) sanity smoke in staging with full network emulation and 2) a controlled rolling upgrade in prod with 10% canary and extended warmup for the KV cache.

[04:40] Priya: For staging smoke, we can mimic port exhaustion but need guidance on throttling thresholds.

[04:55] Sofia: We'll provide a script that simulates ephemeral port exhaustion and a config you can run. Also will include kernel tuning suggestions for the NAT gateway timeouts.

[05:15] Mark: How long of a warmup do we need for the KV cache to hit steady state? We lost a lot of performance in the first 15 minutes last time.

[05:30] Sofia: For your workload mix, I'd estimate 20-30 minutes warmup of active prefixes if you run a synthetic workload that hits the major routes. We can shorten by pre-populating popular prefixes if desired.

[05:55] Daniel: Pre-populating is appealing. Can Redwood give us a dump or seeds to prime the cache?

[06:10] Sofia: Yes, we can export a seed set from the bench traces and share a small loader script. We'll need a secure transfer method, but doable.

[06:30] Priya: Security will want to review any seed data, ensure no PHI in payloads. We'll sanitize.

[06:45] Sara: Yes, please ensure no patient data. Also, for SOC2 scoping — we need docs on key management, audit logs, and network segmentation.

[07:00] Liam: We'll pull our SOC2 pack and send which pages are relevant for the Private install. Expect a pointer to the onboarding security doc.

[07:18] Marco (CSM): Sorry I was late — quick question on the rolling upgrade: do you plan to roll by node or by AZ?

[07:30] Sofia: By node within AZ, to minimize cross-AZ traffic costs and keep KV locality. We'll update the rollout policy to ensure at least one healthy replica with warm cache remains.

[07:55] Priya: During the last upgrade, we observed cross-AZ egress spikes, probably due to pod rescheduling. Any config to prevent that?

[08:12] Sofia: We recommend affinity/anti-affinity hints and preferLocal routing for the cache layer. Also a short drain period to let KV migrate. We'll share suggested k8s pod disruption budgets and preroute filters.

[08:40] Daniel: When you mention preroute filters, are those iptables or a sidecar? We run calico.

[08:55] Sofia: It will be a mix — Calico policies plus iptables rules at the node level for SNAT pools. We don't require a sidecar.

[09:15] Mark: About NAT gateway config — how many ephemeral ports do you suggest per node? We're on AWS and using a single NAT gw per subnet.

[09:30] Sofia: For your concurrency, I'd recommend bumping ephemeral port range and adding a secondary NAT gateway or source natting with per-node egress IPs. That prevents a single gateway bottleneck.

[09:50] Priya: Adding another NAT gw is doable but will increase cost. We'll evaluate.

[10:05] Liam: We'll include cost tradeoffs in the diagram. Also, to reduce retries we can add client-side backoff recommendations in the SDK.

[10:20] Daniel: SDK change is fine but we need to ensure current clients don't flood when they see 5xxs.

[10:35] Sofia: We can ship a small patch and a back-compat config — default conservative backoff.

[10:50] Mark: Okay. Any blockers on our side to start the next smoke?

[11:00] Priya: We need the network diagram and recommended security group rules from Redwood and the script to emulate port exhaustion. Also access to a staging cluster to run the smoke.

[11:15] Liam: We'll send diagram and script today. For staging access, what's the best contact? Priya?

[11:25] Priya: Yes, send it to infra@horizonmedtech.com and cc Sara.

[11:35] Sara: And please include the minimum required IAM roles — we audit those.

[12:00] Marco: Quick note: during the last run, the kubelet logs showed a kernel OOM for one node around the time of the restart. Did you see that?

[12:14] Daniel: I captured logs — it looked like a process leaked file descriptors, but not certain.

[12:25] Sofia: Could be related to the retry storm. We'll correlate with kubelet metrics and open an incident ticket if needed.

[12:38] Mark: Any changes required to the model config for the upgrade?

[12:45] Sofia: No model config changes planned; it's purely infra. We do have a minor runtime patch to improve KV cache lock granularity, but it's backward-compatible. We'll run it in staging first.

[13:05] Priya: Sounds good. For rollout timing, we prefer a weekend window. Targeting week of Aug 17 looks ok.

[13:18] Liam: Great. We'll aim for Aug 17 weekend, propose specific window after staging smoke.

[13:30] Daniel: On benchmarking side, I'll re-run the 128-token avg test and upload the results. Last run is in the shared sheet but we need the same harness with new SDK.

[13:45] Liam: Send the link and we'll validate.

[14:00] Sara: One more security question — has Redwood validated HSM/KMS integrations for private installs? We need the docs.

[14:12] Liam: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS. We'll include the HSM integration guide in the pack.

[14:30] Priya: Perfect. Any competitor notes we should be aware of? Mark: he asked earlier about Bedrock and Anthropic.

[14:40] Mark: We're just benchmarking options. Anthropic's hosted offering is simpler but lacks the private networking. Bedrock has managed endpoints but the performance variability is concerning.

[14:55] Liam: That's useful context. Redwood's strength here is the unified runtime in a customer VPC. We'll highlight the predictability in our doc.

[15:10] Marco: Recap action items — Priya to share logs, Liam to send diagrams, Sofia to run staging smoke and provide scripts, Daniel to re-run benchmarks, Sara to list SOC2 asks.

[15:30] Priya: I'll aim to get logs and route tables by Friday.

[15:40] Daniel: Benchmarks by Monday.

[15:50] Sofia: Smoke tests scheduled for next Tue in staging, will share results.

[16:00] Liam: Ok, unless there's anything else, we'll wrap. Thanks all.

[16:10] Mark: Thanks. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

[16:20] Sara: Thanks everyone.

End of call.

Notes: transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "peer ring" for peering). Links referenced: shared benchmarking sheet (link: https://redwood.example/sheets/pilot-benchmarks), staging scripts repo (link: https://github.com/redwood/pilot-scripts - internal).
